summary: A steel-hard, red insect that has traded its parent's camouflage and flight for armour and a bluff. Scizor's pincers carry eye-like markings that it raises to make itself look three-headed, and they contain steel enough to crush any hard object. Its wings no longer fly; it flaps them fast to regulate its body temperature. It develops from Scyther, a green, grass-hiding ambusher with scythes that cut logs, and in the games only a Scyther traded while holding a Metal Coat becomes one.

anatomy.text: A heavy, winged insect (1.8 m, 118.0 kg) with a body as hard as steel.
Two pincers that contain steel and can crush any hard object they grip; they carry eye-like markings.
Its wings are not used for flying; they are flapped at high speed to adjust body temperature.
anatomy.analogy: Bumblebees and many moths warm up by shivering their flight muscles before they can fly; whether Scizor's flapping warms it or cools it is not said.

anatomy.text: If its steel-hard body conducts heat the way metal does, it would warm and cool quickly, which may be why it needs the wing-flapping.
anatomy.note: A physical guess linking two canon facts; no entry connects them.

diet.text: No entry says what Scizor eats.
Scyther is a predator: it leaps out of tall grass to slice prey, and tears and shreds it with its scythes.
diet.analogy: Praying mantises (Mantodea), which Scyther's category names, are sit-and-wait predators that seize prey with raptorial forelegs.

diet.text: Crushing pincers suit hard-shelled prey, which Scyther's slicing scythes would not; Scizor may take different food from its parent.

habitat.text: Its Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is grassland; Scyther hides in tall grass.
Scizor is not found in the wild in any Gen I-IV game.

In HeartGold and SoulSilver, Scyther appears only during the National Park Bug-Catching Contest (5%), and after the National Pokédex only on Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday contests. In Platinum it is on Routes 210 and 215, commoner in the morning; in Kanto, in the Safari Zone or as a Game Corner prize.

behavior.text: Threat display: it raises its eye-patterned pincers to intimidate, which makes it look three-headed, and it can swing them down dangerously.
Scyther relies on speed: too fast for the eye, leaving only a blur, so fast its opponent doesn't know what hit it, and very proud of it.
Scyther rarely flies; Scizor doesn't fly at all.
Platinum's Scyther are commoner in the morning; no activity pattern is stated for Scizor.

social.text: No entry describes groups. Scyther's speed can create the illusion of more than one, which is a solitary animal looking like many, not a group.

reproduction.text: Bug egg group, even sex ratio, 25 egg cycles (a little longer than most). Nothing is said about breeding or young.

defense.text: A deimatic bluff: the eyespots on its raised pincers make it look like a three-headed animal.
defense.analogy: The peacock butterfly (Aglais io) flashes large eyespots on its wings when disturbed, which experiments show deters small birds.

defense.text: Armour: its steel-hard body is not easily fazed by ordinary attacks.
Scyther's defence was concealment instead: its protective colouring makes it invisible in grass.
Iron Defense (Lv 37) is in Scizor's own level-up list; Swarm or Technician are its abilities.

senses.text: Nothing is said about Scizor's senses. An eyespot display only works on predators that see well, so its enemies are probably visual hunters.

life_cycle.text: Scyther (1.5 m, 56.0 kg, Bug/Flying, green) becomes Scizor (1.8 m, 118.0 kg, Bug/Steel, red) when traded holding a Metal Coat.
The change swaps strategies: from camouflage, speed and slicing scythes to bright colour, a bluff display, crushing pincers and armour; from rare flight to wings used only for heat.
The weight doubles while the height grows only 0.3 m, which fits a body that becomes metal-hard.
Scyther's scythes grow sharper by cutting hard objects; whether that habit feeds into Scizor's steel is not said.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Scizor's level-up list mixes speed and steel: Quick Attack and Bullet Punch (Lv 1), Agility, Metal Claw (Lv 21), Iron Defense (Lv 37), Iron Head (Lv 53).
The cutting moves (Fury Cutter, Slash, X-Scissor, Night Slash) are shared with Scyther and match the scythe canon; in Scizor they come from pincers.
Pursuit (Lv 9) and False Swipe (Lv 13) suit a predator that chases down and holds prey rather than killing at once.
Steel Wing and Roost are machine moves: taught, and of little use to an animal that doesn't fly.

ecology.text: A large insect predator of grassland (trophic level about 3-3.5), if Scizor hunts as Scyther does.
In HeartGold's Bug-Catching Contest, Scyther shares the National Park grass with Butterfree, Beedrill, Caterpie and other contest bugs, only on contest days.

humans.text: People make Scizor: it evolves only by trade, holding a Metal Coat.
Scyther's attacks are nearly impossible to parry, and its scythes cut thick logs in one stroke: dangerous at close quarters.

homestead.text: Breaking hard material: its pincers crush any hard object, useful for stone, nuts or scrap metal at the Works.
Timber and brush clearing is Scyther's job rather than Scizor's: Scyther's scythes slice thick logs in one stroke and cut through grass.
A deterrent at the gate: its three-headed pincer display is built to frighten.
Watch it in Blackthorn's cold: it manages its body temperature by flapping its wings, and how well that works in a highland winter is unknown.
Its size is in the rider range, but it cannot fly and no entry says it carries anyone.
Keep people clear when it swings its pincers down; the display can turn into a strike.

niche.foraging: Scyther: ambush from tall grass and high-speed slashing; Scizor: unknown, perhaps crushing hard prey
niche.note: Scizor's own diet is never stated; the machine reading's herbivore comes from the Bug type alone.

relationships.note: National Park Bug-Catching Contest, HeartGold and SoulSilver (Scyther).

ecotypes.name: Tall-grass reaper
ecotypes.reading: A patient ambusher: Razor Wind takes a turn to charge before it cuts, and Night Slash is a high-critical strike from cover. A lineage that waits in grass and lands one decisive blow, the Yellow canon of leaping out of tall grass in heritable form. Fits dense tall-grass meadow.
ecotypes.behavior: Waits motionless in long grass; one strike, rarely two.

ecotypes.name: Last-stand fencer
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that fights through injury: Endure survives a blow that would knock it out, Reversal hits hardest when it is nearly beaten, and Counter returns physical attacks double. It suits Scizor's armour-and-bluff life, where it holds its ground instead of fleeing. Fits contested open ground where it can't hide.
ecotypes.behavior: Never runs; most dangerous when hurt.

ecotypes.name: Wing-singer
ecotypes.reading: Wings used for sound and wind rather than flight: Bug Buzz is a damaging vibration, Silver Wind a gust of wing scales that can boost all its stats. A lineage that turns Scizor's non-flying, fast-flapping wings into a weapon and display. Fits open meadow where sound carries.
ecotypes.behavior: Buzzes loudly when threatened, before any display of the pincers.

open_questions: What does Scizor eat, and does it still hunt as Scyther does?
Does wing-flapping warm it, cool it, or both (212.2, 212.4)?
How does a Scyther become steel? The games require a held Metal Coat and a trade, neither of which has a wild equivalent.
Is there a wild Scizor population anywhere?
Are the pincer eyespots a bluff against particular predators, and which?
How does it cope with Blackthorn's cold, as a steel-bodied insect that relies on its wings for temperature control?
